verdict.pharmacophore_check: αvβ6: confirm sequence-level pharmacophore in K-01–K-10: RGDL plus D-Pro/N-methyl locks; productive geometry remains unproven. PD-L1: challenge K-01–K-08 PASS claims; aromatic/polar macrocycles are plausible, but the required IgV-cleft chemotype cannot be confirmed from sequences alone.
function_selectivity_concerns: All αvβ6 candidates require functional testing and αvβ3/αvβ5/αvβ8 counterscreens; RGDL and cyclization do not establish selectivity.
All PD-L1 candidates require PD-1/PD-L1 blockade assays; binding alone does not establish checkpoint antagonism.
AVB6-K-04/K-10 charge edits may reduce cationic renal-retention risk, but do not establish lower kidney dose; assess the final labeled conjugate.
AVB6-K-09 flank diversification and PD-L1 tail/Met edits can cause activity cliffs; PASS, LEAD and extended-affinity labels are not experimental evidence.
Trp oxidation remains in AVB6-K-01/K-02/K-04/K-08/K-09/K-10 and every PD-L1 candidate; Met removal does not eliminate oxidation liability.
Hydrophobic clustering warrants solubility/aggregation testing, especially AVB6-K-05/K-08 and PDL1-K-07/K-08; one polarity edit does not establish rescue.
PDL1-K-08 has no free Cys if its disulfide is intact, but reduction/exchange can release thiols and disrupt conformation.
PDL1-K-02 specifies NMeLeu in HELM but Nle in the production note: resolve molecular identity before synthesis.
No N-G/N-S or D-G/D-S hotspots appear, including cyclic junctions; absence does not establish chemical stability.

no_go_before_wetlab.reason: Resolve NMeLeu-versus-Nle identity discrepancy before synthesis/testing.

verdict.overall: HOLD: resolve the identity discrepancy and unverified PD-L1 structural gate; αvβ6 picks are provisional, lower-liability choices for functional/selectivity testing, not validated leads.

verdict.pharmacophore_check: Confirmed. All AVB6 candidates possess the required RGDL selectivity motif + D-Pro/N-methyl lock. All PD-L1 candidates possess the cyclic amphipathic IgV-cleft chemotype.
function_selectivity_concerns: AVB6 selectivity relies strictly on the 'L' and the conformational lock; drastic changes like charge reversals (AVB6-K-04) or multi-residue FTO-dodging (AVB6-K-09) risk distorting the 3D presentation, reverting them to pan-integrin (αvβ3/5/8) bare-RGD binders.
PD-L1 binding is highly structure-gated; sequence swaps (PDL1-K-03, PDL1-K-04) or core polarity shifts (PDL1-K-08) to fix liabilities risk complete loss of function (activity cliffs).
Trp (W) oxidation remains a widespread liability across most candidates (e.g., AVB6-K-08 LEAD, and all PD-L1s).

no_go_before_wetlab.reason: Four simultaneous flank mutations (F->W, A->T, F->H, +NMeGlu) to dodge FTO is a severe activity cliff risk that likely breaks the conformational lock and selectivity.
Swapping D-S to S-D alters the primary sequence and side-chain vectors; high risk of destroying the structure-gated PD-L1 interaction.
Reordering the tail K-D-G to K-G-D alters the local backbone conformation; high activity cliff risk.
Mutating a core hydrophobic Leu to a polar Thr (L->T) to reduce aggregation likely destroys the essential amphipathic IgV-cleft binding.

top_picks: AVB6-K-05 (Maintains RGDL pharmacophore, lacks Trp/Met oxidation liabilities, net charge 0, clean developability)
AVB6-K-07 (Clean developability profile, no Trp/Met, maintains pharmacophore and neutral charge)
PDL1-K-02 (Conservative Met->Leu substitution fixes oxidation while preserving the hydrophobic isostere for cleft binding)
verdict.overall: HOLD pending wet-lab validation of sequence-altered candidates, but GO with top picks AVB6-K-05 and PDL1-K-02 which safely optimize developability without risking activity cliffs.
